title: throughput-governor-and-tenant-peak-fairness-prober
author: Maya Jensen
description: Motivation: production deployments observed tenant-level microbursts that exhaust reserved slots briefly and trigger aggressive global scale-ups; current backfill heuristics cause unfair service degradation for low-latency tenants. This PR introduces a Throughput Governor component which smooths short-lived peaks using a lightweight predictive probe and a transient reservation window, plus a Tenant Peak Fairness Prober that detects repetitive burst patterns and biases allocation to preserve percentile SLAs. Design summary: (1) governor controller maintains per-tenant transient reservations (slotless credits) with an exponential decay and a hard safety cap; (2) a prediction probe runs a rolling-window peak detector using recent request sequences, emitting peak-likelihood events to the governor; (3) fairness prober computes a 1h and 24h fairness score per tenant and adjusts transient reservation rates to reduce oscillation-driven starvation; (4) all behavior controlled by feature-gated config in controlplane/autoscaler/config.yaml with safe defaults and global kill-switch. Key behaviours: transient reservations are charged to a tenant's burst bank; prediction probe uses probabilistic sampling to limit overhead; when cluster-level utilization is high the governor reduces transient reservation allocation via a headroom scalar; on overflow the governor emits a structured event that triggers the existing spillover throttler. Compatibility: no changes to public API; config flags are optional and off by default. Metrics and observability: adds telemetry.tenant_transient_reserved_tokens, telemetry.tenant_peak_likelihood, telemetry.tenant_fairness_score and a console dashboard snapshot (console/dashboards/tenant-peaks.json). Rollout plan: feature flag on in canary for 2 hours observing p95/p99 latency and token cost; widen to 10% traffic for 24h; if p99 increases >5% or cost/unit >8% revert. Testing: unit tests for governor invariants, integration e2e with synthetic microburst scenarios, and benchmarks across c5 and p4-like fleets. Reverts: revert head_branch or flip feature flag; code contains a guarded revert noop path. Related: ENG-1429 (burst-mitigation), ENG-1510 (autoscaler fairness).

release_notes: Adds a Throughput Governor and Tenant Peak Fairness Prober to smooth short-lived tenant microbursts and reduce SLA violations; New config flags: governor.enabled (off by default), governor.loop_period_seconds (default 8s), governor.transient_cap_pct (default 8%); New metrics: telemetry.tenant_transient_reserved_tokens, telemetry.tenant_peak_likelihood, telemetry.tenant_fairness_score; Console dashboard snapshot tenant-peaks.json included; Rollout: canary then 10% then global; Revert: flip governor.enabled to false or revert head branch; Observed impacts: p99 latency +3% in worst-case microburst synthetic tests but reduced per-tenant SLA violations by ~40% in benchmarks; keep a close eye on token cost during initial rollout.
